fichas.title: Keeping Animals: Hands-on and Hands-off Principles
fichas.summary: The page contrasts hands-on animal keeping, involving direct contact among tame animals, keepers and visitors, with hands-off protected contact, developed for safe handling of dangerous animals. It describes functional separation of public and private areas, enclosures, keeper access and subsidiary rooms, emphasizing hygiene, animal presentation, low disturbance, species-appropriate habitats, research and breeding.

fichas.title: Elephant Park, Cologne Zoo
fichas.summary: An integrated hands-off facility combining an animal house and open-air enclosure. The partially roofed area can be divided into sections from a control centre using mechanical gates. Water-filled ditches or level differences separate visitors from the enclosures. The plan labels elephant, bull, pair and cow enclosures, keeper access, a subsidiary room and a water barrier (moat).

fichas.title: Great Ape Facility, Wuppertal Zoo
fichas.summary: An animal house with an outside enclosure built subsequently. The internal enclosure is lit from above and includes protected sleeping bunks. A glass partition separates animals from visitors; keepers access the enclosure from behind. The facility includes a feed kitchen and special cages for sick and baby apes. The plan labels visitor areas, a pond, an infirmary and a care room.

fichas.title: Ozeaneum, Stralsund
fichas.summary: A multifunctional animal house and aquarium with an extensive visitor round tour, thematically divided aquariums and a central keeper area. It serves exhibition and research, with viewing features including a shoal-fish tank, tunnel aquarium, overhead aquarium, touch pools and simulation tanks. The plan labels Baltic and North Sea aquariums, a large shoal-fish basin, exhibition areas, a waiting area and a foyer.
